description:
Found by the fz-kdt.125 refutation (2026-09-01), PRE-EXISTING --
byte-identical at bd03d922e and 41906b046 (not the identity axis).
Two witnesses, probes in session scratchpad (refuter probes/):

(N1) send two closures to self, receive both, P.run(f,10) each:
interp 12 90 (correct); JIT 11 30; AOT 11 30. Same class via
spawn+send to a child. The mailbox-delivered closure is invoked ONCE
where the source says twice (f.(f.(x)) collapses to f.(x)? -- the
11/30 pattern = one application of each reducer).

(N2) send one closure, receive, dbg(f.(10)): interp 11; JIT prints
NOTHING exit 0; AOT prints NOTHING exit 0. Control send(1,7) works on
both doors -- it is the closure crossing the mailbox, not the mailbox.

Three-path parity law violated twice in the closures-x-mailbox
intersection. Triage together; suspect the message-transport path for
callable values (boxing seam at the send/receive boundary vs the
receive type widening past finite callable sets -- see the fz-kdt.125
refutation's receive.rs notes). Related family: fz-kdt.117 (closure
carriers), fz-kdt.99 (threaded-closure interp crash).
title: P1: closures through the mailbox break on JIT/AOT -- invoked once where source says twice; direct invoke prints nothing
